newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Wegener profit jumps, splits shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wegener profit jumps, splits shares.

text.p: Dutch publisher and multimedia group Wegener NV announced an 18 percent jump in 1996 profits on Wednesday, beating expectations and forecast a rise in 1997 earnings per share of at least 10 percent.

The company reported net profits of 69.4 million guilders ($36.8 million), up from 58.7 million one year earlier. In August it said it expected profit growth in the second half of 1996 to match the 16.1 percent growth of the first half.
Wegener also said it proposed to split its shares on a one for five basis but gave no explicit reason for the move.

"It is expected that revenues will grow both autonomously as well as from recent and future acquisitions, and that direct costs might relatively decrease. That constitutes a positive outlook for 1997," the company said in a statement.
Further acquisitions are intended, particularly in the direct marketing and music sectors, it added.
The results and news of the share split were well received by the Amsterdam market, the shares rising 6.00 guilders to 196.50 in early trade, a jump of more than three percent.
The 1996 dividend rose to 3.65 guilders per share from 3.42 guilders in 1995.

The company said it did not expect any alteration in the composition of revenues in 1997 after the "radical change" of last year. It anticipated further growth in advertising revenues from newspaper publishing and acquisitions made late in 1996 would contribute to revenue growth in the music sector.
Wegener said the introduction of new technologoy would result in initial costs during 1997 and that the resultant savings would not be visible until 1998.
"There will be initial costs for implementing new media, including activities on the internet and regional television.

A shut down at a printing plant at Deventer, in the east of the Netherlands would go ahead at the end of 1997 as part of the integration process within the newspaper publishing division. ($ = 1.885 Dutch Guilders)
